nodes.name: Jumping conditions $\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{F_n})$
nodes.statement: We define for a large integer $N$, which depends on $F$, \[ \hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{F_n}) := \left\{x\in\hat{E}(\calO_{F_n}): \Tr_{F_n/F_m}x\in \hat{E}(\calO_{F_{m-1}}))\text{ for all }m\in S_{N,i'}^n \text{ and }\Tr_{F_n/F_N}x=0\right\}, \] where \begin{align*} S_{N,1'}^n&=\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ even}\};\\ S_{N,2'}^n&=\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ odd}\}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Subgroups of $\hat{E}(\calO_{F_n})$ cut out by Kobayashi-type trace ('jumping') conditions along the even/odd levels $S_{N,i'}^n$.

nodes.name: Iwasawa cohomology $H^1_{\Iw}(F,T)$
nodes.statement: For $T\in\Rep_{\ZZ_p}(\calG_F)$, define $H^1_{\Iw}(F,T)=\varprojlim H^1(F_n,T)$ where the connecting maps are corestrictions $\cor_{n/m}:H^1(F_n,T)\rightarrow H^1(F_m,T)$ for $n\ge m$.

nodes.name: $\tilde{\EE}$
nodes.statement: Define \[ \tilde{\EE}=\varprojlim_{x\rightarrow x^p} \CC_p = \left\{ (x^{(0)},x^{(1)},\dots)\mid \left(x^{(i+1)}\right)^p=x^{(i)}\right\},\] and let $\tilde{\EE}^+=\left\{x\in\tilde{\EE}\mid x^{(0)}\in \calO_{\CC_p}\right\}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Fontaine; theory of the field of norms
nodes.statement_short: The tilt $\varprojlim_{x\mapsto x^p}\CC_p$, an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, with its subring $\tilde{\EE}^+$.

nodes.name: $(\vp,\Gamma)$-module $\DD_F(T)$
nodes.statement: For a $p$-adic representation $T\in\Rep_{\ZZ_p}(\calG_{\QQ_p})$ (resp. $V\in\Rep_{\QQ_p}(\calG_{\Qp})$), define $\DD_F(T)=(\AA\otimes_{\ZZ_p}T)^{H_F}$ (resp. $\DD_F(V)=(\BB\otimes_{\QQ_p}V)^{H_F}$).
nodes.statement_short: The $H_F$-invariants of $\AA\otimes T$ (resp. $\BB\otimes V$), a free $\AA_F$-module with commuting $\vp$ and $\Gamma_F$ actions.

nodes.name: Extension of the $\Gamma_F$-action to $G_F$
nodes.statement: If $F_\infty$ is Galois over $\QQ_p$, then the action of $\Gamma_F$ extends to an action of $G_F=\Gal(F_\infty\slash\QQ_p)$. Moreover, the action of $G_F$ commutes with the action of $\vp$.

nodes.name: Overconvergence of $p$-adic representations
nodes.statement: The main result of~\cite{cherbonniercolmez98} shows that every $p$-adic representation $V$ of $\calG_{\QQ_p}$ is overconvergent, i.e. there exists $r(V)>0$ such that \[ \DD_{\QQ_p}(V)=\BB_{\QQ_p}\otimes_{\BB^{\dagger,r(V)}_{\QQ_p}}\DD^{\dagger,r(V)}(V).\]
nodes.statement_short: Every $p$-adic representation of $\calG_{\QQ_p}$ descends to an overconvergent $(\vp,\Gamma)$-module.
assumptions: every $p$-adic representation $V$ of $\calG_{\QQ_p}$
conclusions: is overconvergent, i.e. there exists $r(V)>0$ such that \[ \DD_{\QQ_p}(V)=\BB_{\QQ_p}\otimes_{\BB^{\dagger,r(V)}_{\QQ_p}}\DD^{\dagger,r(V)}(V).\]

nodes.name: The Robba ring $\BB^{\dagger}_{\rig,F}$
nodes.statement: For $n\ge0$, define $\BB^{\dagger,n}_{\rig,F}$ to be the completion of $\BB^{\dagger,n}_{F}$ in the Fr\'echet topology, and define the Robba ring $\BB^{\dagger}_{\rig,F}=\bigcup_n \BB^{\dagger,n}_{\rig,F}$.
nodes.genus: the completion of $\BB^{\dagger,n}_{F}$ in the Fr\'echet topology

nodes.name: Berger's comparison isomorphism
nodes.statement: The most important application of $\BB^\dagger_{\rig,F}$ is Berger's comparison isomorphism: if $V$ is a crystalline representation of $\calG_F$, we write $\DD_{\cris}(V)$ and $\NN(V)$ for the Dieudonn\'{e} module and the Wach module of $V$ respectively, then there is a canonical isomorphism \begin{equation} \iota: \DD^\dagger_F(V)\otimes_{\BB^\dagger_F}\BB^\dagger_{\rig,F}[t^{-1}]\cong \DD_{\cris}(V)\otimes_{F^{\mathrm{nr}}}\BB^\dagger_{\rig,F}[t^{-1}] \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For crystalline $V$ the overconvergent $(\vp,\Gamma)$-module and $\DD_{\cris}(V)$ become isomorphic after $\otimes\BB^\dagger_{\rig,F}[t^{-1}]$.
assumptions: if $V$ is a crystalline representation of $\calG_F$
conclusions: then there is a canonical isomorphism \begin{equation} \iota: \DD^\dagger_F(V)\otimes_{\BB^\dagger_F}\BB^\dagger_{\rig,F}[t^{-1}]\cong \DD_{\cris}(V)\otimes_{F^{\mathrm{nr}}}\BB^\dagger_{\rig,F}[t^{-1}] \end{equation}

nodes.name: The operator $\psi$
nodes.statement: Note that the extension $\EE$ over $\vp(\EE)$ is inseparable of degree $p$. One can hence define a left inverse $\psi$ of $\vp$ on $\AA$. Explicitly, a basis of $\AA$ over $\vp(\AA)$ is given by $1,1+\pi,\dots,(1+\pi)^{p-1}$. For $x\in\AA$, we may write $x=\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}\vp(x_i)(1+\pi)^i$ where $x_i\in\AA$. We set $\psi(x)=x_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The canonical left inverse of $\vp$ on $\AA$, extracted from the expansion of $x$ in the basis $(1+\pi)^i$.

nodes.name: Tate twist $V(m)$
nodes.statement: If $m$ is an integer and $V\in\Rep_{\QQ_p}(\calG_F)$ (resp. $T\in\Rep_{\ZZ_p}(\calG_F)$), we denote by $V(m)$ (resp. $T(m)$) the $\calG_F$-representations $V\otimes_{\Qp}\Qp\cdot e_m$ (resp. $T\otimes_{\Zp}\Zp\cdot e_m$) where $\calG_F$ acts on $e_m$ via $\chi^m$.

nodes.name: The Herr complex $\calC^\bullet_{f,\gamma}(\DD_F(T))$
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma$ be a topological generator of $\Gamma_F$. For $f=\vp$ or $\psi$, define the complex \[ \calC^\bullet_{f,\gamma}\big(\DD_F(T)\big): 0\rightarrow \DD_F(T)\rTo^{\alpha_f}\DD_F(T)\oplus\DD_F(T)\rTo^{\beta_f}\DD_F(T)\rightarrow 0,\] where $\alpha_f(x)=\big((\gamma-1)x,(f-1)x\big)$ and $\beta_f(x,y)=(f-1)x-(\gamma-1)y$. Denote by $H^i\big(\calC^\bullet_{f,\gamma}(\DD_F(V))\big)$ the $i$-th cohomology group of the complex.
nodes.statement_short: The two-step complex computing Galois cohomology from $\DD_F(T)$ via $\gamma-1$ and $f-1$ for $f=\vp$ or $\psi$.

nodes.name: Herr's theorem
nodes.statement: For $f=\vp$ or $\psi$, $H^i\big(\calC^\bullet_{f,\gamma}(\DD_F(T))\big)$ is canonically isomorphic to $H^i(F,T)$. In particular, if $(x,y)\in\DD_F(T)^{\oplus 2}$ satisfies $\beta_\vp(x,y)=0$, then the corresponding cohomology class in $H^1(F,T)$ is given by the cocycle \[ c_{(x,y)}: \sigma\mapsto \frac{\sigma-1}{\gamma-1}x-(\sigma-1)z,\] where $z\in\AA\otimes_{\Zp}T$ is such that $(\vp-1)z=y$.
nodes.statement_short: The Herr complex computes $H^i(F,T)$, with an explicit cocycle formula in degree 1.
assumptions: For $f=\vp$ or $\psi$
if $(x,y)\in\DD_F(T)^{\oplus 2}$ satisfies $\beta_\vp(x,y)=0$
conclusions: then the corresponding cohomology class in $H^1(F,T)$ is given by the cocycle \[ c_{(x,y)}: \sigma\mapsto \frac{\sigma-1}{\gamma-1}x-(\sigma-1)z,\] where $z\in\AA\otimes_{\Zp}T$ is such that $(\vp-1)z=y$.

nodes.name: Iwasawa-cohomology comparison $H^1_{\Iw}(F,T)\cong\DD_F(T)^{\psi=1}$
nodes.statement: We have an $\Lambda(\Gamma_F)$-equivariant isomorphism $H^1_{\Iw}(F,T)\cong\DD_{F}(T)^{\psi=1}$. If $F_\infty$ is Galois over $\Qp$, then the isomorphism is compatible with the action of $G=\Gal(F_\infty\slash \Qp)$.
nodes.statement_short: Iwasawa cohomology is computed by the $\psi=1$ part of the $(\vp,\Gamma)$-module, equivariantly for $G$.
assumptions: If $F_\infty$ is Galois over $\Qp$
conclusions: then the isomorphism is compatible with the action of $G=\Gal(F_\infty\slash \Qp)$.

nodes.name: Proof of the comparison theorem
nodes.statement: See \cite[Th\'eor\`eme II.1.3]{cherbonniercolmez99}.
nodes.statement_short: Cited from Cherbonnier-Colmez.

nodes.name: $a_p=0$
nodes.statement: Assume throughout this section that $a_p=0$.

nodes.name: $\log^\pm(1+\pi)$
nodes.statement: Define $\log^-(1+\pi)=\prod_{i\geq 0}\frac{\vp^{2i}(q)}{p}$ and $\log^+(1+\pi)=\prod_{i\geq 0}\frac{\vp^{2i+1}(q)}{p}$, which are elements of $\BB^+_{\rig,\Qp}$.

nodes.name: Change-of-basis matrix $M$ for $\NN(T)$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} M= \begin{pmatrix} \log^-(1+\pi) & 0 \\ 0 & \log^+(1+\pi) \end{pmatrix}.\end{equation}

nodes.name: Relation between the $v$- and $n$-coordinates
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} x_1=x_1'\log^-(1+\pi)\quad\text{and}\quad x_2=x_2'\log^+(1+\pi). \end{equation}

nodes.name: $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$ and $H^1(K_n,T)^i$
nodes.statement: For $i=1,2$, let \[ H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i=\left\{x\in\DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}:\vp(x_i)=-p\psi(x_i)\right\}.\] For $n\geq 1$, define $H^1(K_n,T)^i$ to be the image of $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$ under the natural projection map $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)\rightarrow H^1(K_n,T)$.
nodes.statement_short: The signed local conditions: elements of $\DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$ whose $i$-th coordinate satisfies $\vp(x_i)=-p\psi(x_i)$, and their images at finite level.

nodes.name: Relation to the Coleman maps
nodes.statement: As show in~\cite[\S 5.2.1]{leiloefflerzerbes10}, we have $H^1_{\Iw}(\Qp,T)^i=H^1_{\Iw}(\Qp,T)\cap\ker(\underline{\Col}_i)$ for the Coleman maps \[ \underline{\Col}_i: H^1_{\Iw}(\Qp,T)\rTo\Lambda(\Gamma)\] defined in {\em op.cit.}

nodes.name: $H^1_{f,i}(K_n,\Ep)$
nodes.statement: Let $H^1_{f,i}(K_n,\Ep)$ be the orthogonal complement of $H^1(K_n,T)^i$ under the Pontryagin duality \[ [\sim,\sim]: H^1(K_n,T)\times H^1(K_n,\Ep)\rTo \Qp\slash\Zp\] for $i=1,2$.
nodes.genus: the orthogonal complement of $H^1(K_n,T)^i$ under the Pontryagin duality

nodes.name: $J^i_v(L_n)$ and $J^i_v(L_\infty)$
nodes.statement: Let $i=1,2$. For all $v\in S$, define \[ J^i_v(L_n)= \bigoplus_{w_n\mid v} \frac{H^1(L_{w_n,n},\Ep)}{H^1_{f,i}(L_{w_n,n},\Ep)},\] where the direct sum is taken over all primes $w_n$ of $L_n$ above $v$ and $H^1_{f,i}(L_{w_n,n},\Ep)=H^1_f(L_{w_n,n},\Ep)$ whenever $v\neq p$. We write $J^i_v(L_\infty)=\varinjlim J^i_v(L_n)$.
nodes.statement_short: The local quotient terms of the signed Selmer group, using $H^1_{f,i}$ at $p$ and the usual $H^1_f$ elsewhere.

nodes.name: Signed Selmer group $\Sel^i(E\slash L_\infty)$
nodes.statement: For $i=1,2$, define \[ \Sel^i(E\slash L_\infty)=\ker\left( H^1(G_S(L_\infty),\Ep)\rTo \bigoplus_{v\in S}J^i_v(L_\infty)\right).\]

nodes.name: Coleman maps $\Col_i$ and $\underline{\Col}_i$
nodes.statement: In \cite{leiloefflerzerbes10}, we have defined two pairs of Coleman maps (with respect to the chosen basis), \begin{align*} \Col_i:\NN(V)^{\psi=1} & \rTo(\BB_{\Qp}^+)^{\psi=0}, \hspace{3ex}\text{and} \\ \underline{\Col}_i:\NN(V)^{\psi=1} & \rTo\Lambda_{\Qp}(\Gamma) \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Two pairs of maps out of $\NN(V)^{\psi=1}$, landing in $(\BB^+_{\Qp})^{\psi=0}$ and in $\Lambda_{\Qp}(\Gamma)$.

nodes.name: Defining property of the Coleman maps
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: $(1-\vp)(x)$ expanded in the $\bar{\nu}$-basis has the $\Col_i(x)$ (resp. $\underline{\Col}_i(x)$) as coordinates.

nodes.name: $H^1(\QQ_{p,n},T)^i$ in the ordinary case
nodes.statement: Let $H^1(\QQ_{p,n},T)^i$ be the image of $\ker(\underline{\Col}_i)\cap\NN(T)^{\psi=1}$ under the natural maps $\NN(T)^{\psi=1}\rightarrow H^1_{\Iw}(\Qp,T)\rightarrow H^1(\QQ_{p,n},T)$ and write $H^1_{f,i}(\QQ_{p,n},\Ep)$ for the exact annihilator of $H^1(\QQ_{p,n},T)^i$ under the Tate pairing.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: $\Sel^i(E/\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))$ in the ordinary case
nodes.statement: Define \[ \Sel^i(E/\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))=\ker\left(\Sel(E/\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))\rightarrow \frac{H^1(\Qp(\mu_{p^n}),\Ep)}{H^1_{f,i}(\Qp(\mu_{p^n}),\Ep)})\right) \] where $\Sel(E/\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))$ denotes the usual Selmer group and we define $\Sel^i(E/\QQ(\mu_{p^\infty}))$ to be the direct limit of $\Sel^i(E/\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Normalisation of the basis vector $\bar{n}_2$
nodes.statement: We can choose $\bar{n}_2$ such that $u=\alpha^{-1}$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
assumptions: for some $u\in (\BB^+_{\QQ_p})^\times$ which is congruent to $\alpha^{-1}\mod \pi$

nodes.name: Proof of the basis normalisation
nodes.statement: If we let $\bar{n}_1'=\bar{n}_1$ and $\bar{n}_2'=v\bar{n}_2$ where $v\in(\BB_{\Qp}^+)^\times$, then $\bar{n}_1',\bar{n}_2'$ is also a basis of $\NN(V(-1))$. The matrix of $\vp$ with respect to this basis is of the form \[ P'=\begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \star \\ 0 & v^{-1}\vp(v)uq \end{pmatrix}.\] Note that $\alpha u\equiv1\mod\pi$ implies that $\vp^n(\alpha u)\rightarrow 1$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the product $\prod_{n\ge0}\vp^n(\alpha u)$ converges to an element $u'\in(\BB_{\Qp}^+)^\times$. Since $u'\vp(u')^{-1}=\alpha u$, we deduce that $P'$ is of the required form if we take $v=u'$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Rescale $\bar{n}_2$ by the convergent product $u'=\prod_{n\ge0}\vp^n(\alpha u)$, which satisfies $u'\vp(u')^{-1}=\alpha u$.

nodes.name: Description of $\ker(\underline{\Col}_2)$ in the $\bar{n}$-basis
nodes.statement: With respect to the basis given by Lemma~\ref{basis}, \[ \ker(\underline{\Col}_2)=\left\{x\in\NN(V)^{\psi=1}|\vp(x_2)=\alpha x_2\text{ where }x=(x_1\bar{n}_1+x_2\bar{n}_2)\otimes \pi^{-1}e_1\text{ with } x_i\in\BB_{\Qp}^+\right\}. \]
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: $\ker(\underline{\Col}_2)$ consists of the $x$ whose $\bar{n}_2$-coordinate satisfies $\vp(x_2)=\alpha x_2$.
assumptions: With respect to the basis given by Lemma~\ref{basis}

nodes.name: Proof of the description of $\ker(\underline{\Col}_2)$
nodes.statement: By \eqref{colemanmaps}, we have $\Col_2(x)=\alpha x_2-\vp(x_2)$. Moreover, $M$ is lower triangular with $\alpha\frac{t}{\pi q}$ and $\alpha^{-1}$ on the diagonal. Therefore, $\ker(\underline{\Col}_2)=\ker(\Col_2)$ and we are done.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\Col_2(x)=\alpha x_2-\vp(x_2)$ and note $M$ is lower triangular with unit diagonal, so the two kernels agree.

nodes.name: Description of $\ker(\underline{\Col}_2)$ in the $\bar{\nu}$-basis
nodes.statement: With respect to the basis given by Lemma~\ref{basis}, \[ \ker(\underline{\Col}_2)=\left\{x\in\NN(V)^{\psi=1}|\vp(x_2)=\alpha x_2\text{ where }x=(x_1\bar{\nu}_1+x_2\bar{\nu}_2)\otimes t^{-1}e_1 \text{ with } x_i\in\Brig\right\}. \]
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: The same kernel description transported to the Dieudonn\'e-module basis via $t^{-1}e_1$.
assumptions: With respect to the basis given by Lemma~\ref{basis}

nodes.name: Proof of the $\bar{\nu}$-basis description
nodes.statement: This follows from Lemma~\ref{firstform} and \eqref{secondform}.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Change of coordinates in Lemma firstform.

nodes.name: $J^2_v(L_n)$ and $\Sel^2(E\slash L_\infty)$ in the ordinary case
nodes.statement: For all $v\in S$, define \[ J^2_v(L_n)= \bigoplus_{w_n\mid v} \frac{H^1(L_{w_n,n},\Ep)}{H^1_{f,2}(L_{w_n,n},\Ep)},\] where the direct sum is taken over all primes $w_n$ of $L_n$ above $v$. Here, $H^1_{f,2}(L_{w_n,n},\Ep)=H^1_f(L_{w_n,n},\Ep)$ whenever $v\nmid p$. Define $J^{2}_v(L_\infty)=\varinjlim J^{(2)}_v(L_n)$. Define \[ \Sel^2(E\slash L_\infty)=\ker\left( H^1(G_S(L_\infty),\Ep)\rightarrow \bigoplus_{v\in S}J^2_v(L_\infty)\right).\]
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Only the trivial solution of $ax=\vp(x)$
nodes.statement: Let $a\in \ZZ_p^\times$, and assume that $a$ is not a root of unity. If $x\in\BB^\dagger_{\rig,K}$ satisfies \begin{equation} a x-\vp(x)=0 \end{equation} then $x=0$.
assumptions: Let $a\in \ZZ_p^\times$, and assume that $a$ is not a root of unity.
If $x\in\BB^\dagger_{\rig,K}$ satisfies \begin{equation} a x-\vp(x)=0 \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof that $ax=\vp(x)$ forces $x=0$
nodes.statement:
If $x\in \Brig$, then we can substitute $\pi=e^t-1$ to write $x$ of the form $\sum_{n\geq 0}c_nt^n$ with $c_n\in\QQ_p$. Since $\vp(t)=pt$, it is clear from this description that for any $a
eq 1$ and $x
e0$, we have $\vp(x)
eq ax$. Let $x\in\BB^\dagger_{ig,\Qp}-\Brig$. Assume that there exists $n\ge 0$ be such that $x\in \BB^{\dagger,n}_{ig,\QQ_p}$ and $x
ot\in \BB^{\dagger,n-1}_{ig,\QQ_p}$. Then $\vp(x)\in \BB^{\dagger,n+1}_{ig,\QQ_p}-\BB^{\dagger,n}_{ig,\QQ_p}$, so $\vp(x)
eq a x$. If $x\in\BB^{\dagger,n}_{ig,\QQ_p}$ for all $n\ge0$ and $x
ot\in\Brig$, then $\vp^{-1}(x)$ converges in $\BB^+_{\mathrm{dR}}$, so if we write $x=f(\pi)$, then $f(T)$ does not have a pole at $\varepsilon^{(1)}-1$. But $f(T)$ has a pole at $T=0$ as $x
ot\in\Brig$, so $f ig( (T+1)^p-1 ig)$ has poles at the $\{(\varepsilon^{(1)})^i-1:0\leq i<p\}$. Hence $\vp(x)
eq ax$. Assume now that $x\in \BB^\dagger_{ig,K}$ satisfies $\vp(x)=ax$, and that $x
ot\in \BB^{\dagger}_{ig,\QQ_p}$. On replacing $K$ by its Galois closure, if necessary, we may assume that $K\slash\QQ_p$, and hence $K_{\infty}\slash\QQ_{p,\infty}$, are Galois. Let $H=\Gal(K_{\infty}\slash \QQ_{p,\infty})$. Since $\vp$ is $H$-equivariant, $\sigma(x)$ also satisfies~\eqref{nosolution} for all $\sigma\in H$. More generally, if $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_i\in H$, then $y=\sigma_1(x_2)\dots\sigma_i(x_2)$ satisfies $a^iy=\vp(y)$. The coefficients of the polynomial \[ f(Y)=\prod_{\sigma\in H} (Y-\sigma(x))\] are elements in $\BB^{\dagger}_{ig,\QQ_p}$ which satisfy an equation of the form~\eqref{nosolution}, so they must all be zero by the above argument. But the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\BB^\dagger_{ig,\QQ_p}$ divides $f(Y)$, which gives a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis over the levels $\BB^{\dagger,n}_{\rig,\QQ_p}$, then Galois descent from $K$ to $\QQ_p$ ending in a contradiction with minimality.

nodes.name: The unit root $\alpha$ is not a root of unity
nodes.statement: The unit root $\alpha$ of the polynomial $X^2-a_pX+p$ is a Weil number of complex absolute value $\sqrt{p}$, so it cannot be a root of unity.

nodes.name: Membership in $H^1_{\Iw}(K_\nu,T)^2$ means $x_2=0$
conclusions: Then $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K_\nu,T)^2$ if and only if $x_2=0$.

nodes.name: Proof that $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K_\nu,T)^2$ iff $x_2=0$
nodes.statement: Immediate from Lemma~\ref{onlytrivialsolution} and Remark~\ref{Weilnumber}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the vanishing lemma with the fact that $\alpha$ is a Weil number.

nodes.name: $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^2=\DD_K(\hat{T})^{\psi=1}$
nodes.statement: $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^2$ if and only if $x\in \DD_{K}(\hat{T})^{\psi=1}$.
assumptions: To simplify notation, let $K=L_\nu$.

nodes.name: Proof that $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^2$ is the formal-group part
nodes.statement: It follows immediately from the comparison isomorphism and the fact that $\bar{\nu}_1=\bar{n}_1$ that any $x\in\DD_{K}(T)^{\psi=1}$ which satisfies $\iota(x)=x_1\bar{\nu}_1\otimes t^{-1}e_1$ must indeed lie in $\DD_{K}(\hat{T})$.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the comparison isomorphism and $\bar{\nu}_1=\bar{n}_1$.

nodes.name: $\Sel(E\slash L_\infty)=\Sel^2(E\slash L_\infty)$
nodes.statement: We have $\Sel(E\slash L_\infty)=\Sel^2(E\slash L_\infty)$.
assumptions: let $E$ be an elliptic curve defined over $\QQ$ with good ordinary reduction at a prime $p\geq 3$
Let $L$ be a finite extension of $\QQ$, and let $L_\infty=L(\mu_{p^\infty})$.

nodes.name: Proof that the ordinary $\Sel^2$ is the usual Selmer group
nodes.statement_short: Identify $H^1_{\Iw}(L_\nu,\hat{T})$ with $\varprojlim H^1_f$ via Perrin-Riou and Bloch-Kato, then dualize.

nodes.name: $\AA^{\dagger,n}_K$ as a $p$-adic completion
nodes.statement: For all $n\geq N_K$, $\AA^{\dagger,n}_K$ is the $p$-adic completion of $\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]\cap\AA^{\dagger,n}_K$.
assumptions: For all $n\geq N_K$

nodes.name: Proof of the completion description
nodes.statement: Note that the condition that $\sum_{k\in\ZZ}a_kX^k$ is holomorphic and bounded above by $1$ on the annulus $p^{-1/e_Kp^{n-1}(p-1)}\leq\mid X\mid<1$ is equivalent to the condition that \[ v_p(a_k)+\frac{k}{e_K(p-1)p^{n-1}}\geq 0 \hspace{2ex} \text{and $\rightarrow +\infty$ as $k\rightarrow -\infty$}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Translate the holomorphy-and-boundedness condition on the annulus into valuation inequalities on the coefficients.

nodes.name: Vanishing criterion via $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}$
nodes.statement: Let $x\in\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ where $N\ge N_K$. If $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)=0$ for infinitely many $n\ge N$, then $x=0$.
assumptions: Let $x\in\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ where $N\ge N_K$.
If $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)=0$ for infinitely many $n\ge N$

nodes.name: Proof of the vanishing criterion
nodes.statement: Firstly, we assume that $x\in\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]$. We write $\sigma$ for the Frobenious in $\Gal(K'/\Qp)$. Let \[ F(X)=\sum_{m\ge -r}b_mX^m\in\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![X]\!][X^{-1}] \] such that $F(\pi_K)=x$. For $i=1,\ldots,[K':\Qp]$, write \[ F_i(X)=\sum_{m\ge -r}\sigma^i(b_m)X^m.\] Then $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)=F_i(\pi_{n})$, where $i+n\equiv0\mod[K':\Qp]$ and $\pi_n=\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(\pi_K)$. Therefore, there exists an $i$ such that $F_i$ has infinitely many zeros. But $F_i\in X^{-r}\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![X]\!]$, so $F_i=0$ by the Weierstrass preparation theorem. This implies that $b_m=0$ for all $m$, so $x=0$. To conclude, note that if $n\ge N$, $\{x\in\AA^{\dagger,N}_K:\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)=0\}$ is a closed set of $\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ under the $p$-adic topology and $\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ is the $p$-adic completion of $\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]\cap\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ by Lemma~\ref{completion}.
nodes.statement_short: Weierstrass preparation kills a Laurent series with infinitely many zeros; then pass to the $p$-adic completion.

nodes.name: Compatibility of $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}$ with traces
nodes.statement: Let $n\gg0$ and $x\in\BB_{K}^{\dagger,n}$, then \[ \Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ \theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)=\theta\circ\vp^{-n}\circ\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}(x). \]
assumptions: Let $n\gg0$ and $x\in\BB_{K}^{\dagger,n}$

nodes.name: Proof of the trace compatibility
nodes.statement: We let $n$ be an integer such that $[K_n:K_{n-1}]=p$ and $n\ge a(K)+1$ where $a(K)$ is the integer as in \cite[Proposition~III.2.1]{cherbonniercolmez99}. Write \[ x=\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}[\varepsilon]^i\vp(x_i) \] where $x_i\in\BB_{K}^{\dagger,n-1}$. Then, \[ \theta\circ\vp^{-n+1}(x_i)\in K_{n-1} \] for all $i$. Therefore, \begin{eqnarray*} \Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ \theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)&=&\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}\zeta_{p^n}^i\theta\circ\vp^{1-n}(x_i)\right)\\ &=&p\theta\circ\vp^{1-n}(x_0). \end{eqnarray*} But we have $\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}(x)=p\vp(x_0)$, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $x$ in the $[\varepsilon]^i\vp(x_i)$ basis and compute both sides of the trace identity.

nodes.name: Trace relations for the coordinates $x_1,x_2$
nodes.statement: Let $x\in \DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$, then \[\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_1)=-\theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_1)\] for all odd integers $n\ge N+2$ and \[\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_2)=-\theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_2)\] for all even integers $n\ge N+2$.
nodes.statement_short: Each coordinate of $x\in\DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$ satisfies a trace relation, for $n$ of the appropriate parity.
assumptions: Let $x\in \DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$

nodes.name: Proof of the trace relations
nodes.statement: By definitions, we have $\vp(\log^+(1+\pi))=\frac{p}{q}\log^-(1+\pi)$ and $\vp(\log^-(1+\pi))=\log^+(1+\pi)$, and that similar relations hold when replacing $\vp$ by $\psi$. The relations \eqref{basechange} therefore imply that \begin{eqnarray} \vp(x_1)+p\psi(x_1)&=&\left(\vp(x_1')+\psi(qx_1')\right)\log^+(1+\pi);\\ \vp(x_2)+p\psi(x_2)&=&\left(\vp(x_2')+q\psi(x_2')\right)p/q\log^-(1+\pi). \end{eqnarray} If $n\ge 2$ is an even integer, then $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}\left(\log^+(1+\pi)\right)=0$. Therefore, \eqref{log1} implies that \[ \theta\circ\vp^{-n+1}(x_1)+\theta\circ\vp^{-n-1}\left(p\vp\circ\psi(x_1)\right)=0. \] Recall that $p\vp\circ\psi=\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}$, so Lemma~\ref{comptrace} implies the first part of the lemma. Similarly, the second half the lemma follows from \eqref{log2} and the fact that \[\theta\circ\vp^{-n}\left(p/q\log^-(1+\pi)\right)=0\] for all odd integers $n\ge 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\vp(\log^\pm(1+\pi))$ identities and the vanishing of $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(\log^\pm)$ at the right parity.

nodes.name: Trace characterisation of $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$
nodes.statement: Let $x\in \DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$, then $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$ if and only if \[\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_i)=-\theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_i)\] for all $n\ge N+2$.
nodes.statement_short: $x$ lies in the signed local condition exactly when the trace relation holds for all $n\ge N+2$.
assumptions: Let $x\in \DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$
conclusions: then $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$ if and only if \[\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_i)=-\theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_i)\] for all $n\ge N+2$.

nodes.name: Proof of the trace characterisation
nodes.statement: If $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$, then \[ \vp^2(x_i)=-p\vp\circ\psi(x_i)=-\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}(x_i). \] On applying $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}$ to both sides, we have by Lemma~\ref{comptrace} that \[ \theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_i)=-\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_i) \] as required. Conversely, we assume that \[ \Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_i)=-\theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_i) \] for all $n\ge N+2$. Then $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}\left(\vp(x_i)+p\psi(x_i)\right)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{comptrace}. Our assumption implies that $\vp(x_1')+\psi(qx_1')=0$ for $i=1$ and $\vp(x_2')+q\psi(x_2')=0$ for $i=2$ by Lemma~\ref{vanish} and the equations \eqref{log1} and \eqref{log2}. Therefore, we have $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$ as required.
nodes.statement_short: Apply $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}$ to the defining relation for one direction; for the converse use the vanishing lemma.

nodes.name: Parity refinement of the trace characterisation
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{triv0}, we can rewrite Proposition \ref{des1} as follows: \begin{eqnarray*} H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^1&=&\left\{x\in \DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}:\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_1)=-\theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_1)\text{ for all even }n\ge N+2\right\};\\ H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^2&=&\left\{x\in \DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}:\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_2)=-\theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_2)\text{ for all odd }n\ge N+2\right\}. \end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: Description of $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$ via $\exp^*$
nodes.statement: We have \begin{eqnarray*} H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^1&=&\left\{x\in \DD_K(T)^{\psi=1}:\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)\in K_{n-1}\cdot v_1\text{ for all odd }n\ge N+1\right\},\\ H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^2&=&\left\{x\in \DD_K(T)^{\psi=1}:\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)\in K_{n-1}\cdot v_1\text{ for all even }n\ge N+1\right\}. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: The signed conditions say the dual exponential of $x$ lands in $K_{n-1}\cdot v_1$ at every level of the given parity.
assumptions: Let $x\in \DD^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$. Then as in Section~\ref{supersingular}, we can write \[x=x_1v_1+x_2v_2=x_1'n_1+x_2'n_2\] with $x_i\in\BB^{\dagger,N}_{\rig,K}$ and $x_i'\in \BB^{\dagger,N}_{K}$ for $i=1,2$.
conclusions: H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^1&=&\left\{x\in \DD_K(T)^{\psi=1}:\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)\in K_{n-1}\cdot v_1\text{ for all odd }n\ge N+1\right\}
H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^2&=&\left\{x\in \DD_K(T)^{\psi=1}:\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)\in K_{n-1}\cdot v_1\text{ for all even }n\ge N+1\right\}

nodes.name: Proof of the $\exp^*$ description
nodes.statement: By \cite[Th\'eor\`eme IV.2.1]{cherbonniercolmez99}, \[ \exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)= \partial_V\circ \vp^{-n}(x)\] for all $n\geq N$. Since \[ \partial_V\circ \vp^{-n}(x)=\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_1)\vp^{-n}(v_1)+\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_2)\vp^{-n}(v_2)\] and the image of $\exp^*_{K_n}$ lies in $K_n\otimes{\Fil}^0\DD_{\cris}(V)$, it follows that \[ \exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)= \begin{cases} (-1)^mp^{-m}\theta\circ\vp^{-2m}(x_1)v_1 & \text{ if $n=2m\ge N$}, \\ (-1)^mp^{-m}\theta\circ\vp^{-(2m+1)}(x_2)v_1 & \text{ if $n=2m+1\ge N$}. \end{cases} \] Extend the trace map $\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}$ to the map $\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\mathrm{id}$ on $K_n\otimes_{\Qp}\DD_{\cris}(V)$. Then, $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^1$ if and only if \[ \Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)=p^{-1}\exp^*_{K_{n-2}}\circ h^1_{\Iw,{n-2}}(x) \] for all even $n\ge N+2$. But \[ \Tr_{K_m\slash K_{m-1}}\circ \exp^*_{K_{m}} =\exp^*_{K_{m-1}}\circ {\cor}_{K_m\slash K_{m-1}} \] for all $m\ge0$, so we deduce that $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^1$ if and only if \[ \exp^*_{K_{n-1}}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n-1}(x)=p^{-1}\Tr_{K_{n-1}/K_{n-2}}\circ\exp^*_{K_{n-1}}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n-1}(x) \] for all even $n\ge N-2$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Cherbonnier-Colmez's formula for $\exp^*\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}$, split by parity, and use compatibility of $\exp^*$ with corestriction.

nodes.name: $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$ as an inverse limit of finite-level conditions
nodes.statement: For $i\in\{1,2\}$ and $n\geq N+1$, define \[ H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}=\left\{x\in H^1(K_n,T):\Tr_{K_n\slash K_m}\circ\exp^*_{K_n}(x)\in K_{m-1}\cdot v_1\hspace{2ex}\text{for all $m\in S_{N,i}^n$}\right\}.\] where $S_{N,i}^n$ is given by \begin{eqnarray*} S_{N,1}^n&=&\left\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ odd }\right\},\\ S_{N,2}^n&=&\left\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ even }\right\}. \end{eqnarray*} Then $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i=\varprojlim H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$.
nodes.statement_short: The signed local condition is the inverse limit of the finite-level jumping conditions $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$.
assumptions: For $i\in\{1,2\}$ and $n\geq N+1$, define \[ H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}=\left\{x\in H^1(K_n,T):\Tr_{K_n\slash K_m}\circ\exp^*_{K_n}(x)\in K_{m-1}\cdot v_1\hspace{2ex}\text{for all $m\in S_{N,i}^n$}\right\}.\] where $S_{N,i}^n$ is given by \begin{eqnarray*} S_{N,1}^n&=&\left\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ odd }\right\},\\ S_{N,2}^n&=&\left\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ even }\right\}. \end{eqnarray*}

nodes.name: Proof of the finite-level description
nodes.statement: Immediate from Corollary~\ref{trace}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Corollary trace.

nodes.name: $F_n^{(0)}$ and the decomposition of $F_n$
nodes.statement: For an integer $n\ge1$, we write $F_n^{(0)}=\ker(\Tr_{F_n/F_{n-1}})$. Then we have \begin{equation} F_n=F\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^nF_i^{(0)}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ as a preimage under $\exp^*$
nodes.statement: Let $n\ge N+1$ be an integer, then \[ H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}=\left(\exp^*_{K_n}\right)^{-1}\left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\cdot v_1\right) \] where $\{i'\}=\{1,2\}\setminus\{i\}$.
assumptions: Let $n\ge N+1$ be an integer
where $\{i'\}=\{1,2\}\setminus\{i\}$

nodes.name: Proof of the preimage description
nodes.statement: Let $x\in K_n$. By definition, the projection of $x$ under \eqref{pro} into $K_m^{(0)}$ is zero if and only if $\Tr_{K_n/K_{m}}x\in K_{m-1}$. Hence the result.
nodes.statement_short: The $K_m^{(0)}$-component of $x$ vanishes exactly when $\Tr_{K_n/K_m}x\in K_{m-1}$.

nodes.name: $E(K_\infty)$ has no $p$-torsion
nodes.statement: $E(K_\infty)$ has no $p$-torsion.

nodes.name: Consequence of the no-$p$-torsion assumption
nodes.statement: Assumption~\ref{assumptionptorsion} implies that the natural map $H^1(K_n,T)\rTo H^1(K_n,V)$ is injective for all $n\ge0$. In particular, we may embed $H^1(K_n,T)$ into $H^1(K_n,V)$ and consider the former as a lattice inside the latter.

nodes.name: The exact annihilator $H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$
nodes.statement: Let $H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$ be the exact annihilator of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ under the Tate pairing. Then \[ H_{f,N,(i)}^1(K_n,T) = H^1(K_n,T)\cap \exp_{K_n}\left( \bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)} \otimes\DD_{\cris}(V) \right) \]
nodes.statement_short: The annihilator of the jumping condition is the image under $\exp_{K_n}$ of the complementary sum of $K_m^{(0)}$.
assumptions: Let $H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$ be the exact annihilator of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ under the Tate pairing.

nodes.name: Proof of the annihilator description
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{3des}, we have \begin{equation} H^1_{f,N,(1)}(K_n,T)=\left(\left(\exp^*_{K_n}\right)^{-1}\left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\cdot v_1\right)\right)^{\bot_{[,]}} \end{equation} where $(\star)^{\bot_{[,]}}$ denotes the exact annihilator of $\star$ under the pairing $[\sim,\sim]$. But \[ [\exp_{K_n}(\sim),\sim]=\Tr_{K_n/\Qp}\langle\sim,\exp^*_{K_n}(\sim)\rangle. \] where $\langle\sim,\sim\rangle$ is the pairing \[ \langle\sim,\sim\rangle:\Big(K_n\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V)\Big)\times\Big(K_n\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V)\Big)\rightarrow K_n. \] Therefore, \begin{equation} x\in\left(\left(\exp^*_{K_n}\right)^{-1}\left(\star\cdot v_1\right)\right)^{\bot_{[,]}}\quad\text{if and only if}\quad x\in\exp_{K_n}\left((\star)^\bot\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V)\right) \end{equation} where $(\star)^\bot$ denotes the orthogonal complement of $\star$ under the pairing \begin{align*} K_n\times K_n &\rightarrow \Qp\\ (x,y) &\mapsto \Tr_{K_n/\Qp}(xy). \end{align*} By linear algebra, we have \[ \left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\right)^\bot=\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}. \] Hence the result on combining \eqref{E} with \eqref{ortho}.
nodes.statement_short: Adjunction between $\exp$ and $\exp^*$ under the Tate pairing turns the annihilator into an orthogonal complement, computed by linear algebra.

nodes.name: $H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$ via the projection $P_{N,i}^n$
nodes.statement: For $i=1,2$, we have \[ H_{f,N,(i)}^1(K_n,T) = \left\{x\in H_{f}^1(K_n,T):\left(P_{N,i}^n\otimes{\rm id}\right)\circ\exp_{K_n}^{-1}(x)=0\right\}. \]
assumptions: By \eqref{pro}, we may define a projection map \[ P_{N,i}^n:K_n\rTo K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_m^{(0)}. \]

nodes.name: Proof of the projection form
nodes.statement: Note that \[ K_n=\left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_m^{(0)}\right)\oplus\left( \bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\right). \] Therefore, \[ \left(P_{N,i}^n\otimes{\rm id}\right)\circ\exp_{K_n}^{-1}(x)=0\quad\text{if and only if}\quad\exp_{K_n}^{-1}(x)\in \bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V)/\Fil^0\DD_{\cris}(V). \]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the membership condition using the direct-sum decomposition of $K_n$.

nodes.name: The jumping conditions $\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{K_n})$
nodes.statement: For $i\in\{1,2\}$, the image of $H_{f,N,(i)}^1(K_n,T)$ inside $\hat{E}(\calO_{K_n})$ coincides with \begin{align*} \hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{K_n}) :=& \left\{x\in\hat{E}(\calO_{K_n}): \Tr_{K_n/K_m}x\in \hat{E}(\calO_{K_{m-1}})\text{ for all }m\in S_{N,i'}^n \text{ and }\Tr_{K_n/K_N}x=0\right\}\\ =&\left\{x\in\hat{E}(\calO_{K_n}):P_{N,i}^n\circ\log_{\hat{E}}(x)=0\right\}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Inside the formal group, the annihilator is cut out by Kobayashi-style trace conditions.
assumptions: If we identify the image of $\hat{E}(\calO_{K_n})$ under $\delta$ with $H^1_f(K_n,T)$
conclusions: the image of $H_{f,N,(i)}^1(K_n,T)$ inside $\hat{E}(\calO_{K_n})$ coincides with \begin{align*} \hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{K_n}) :=& \left\{x\in\hat{E}(\calO_{K_n}): \Tr_{K_n/K_m}x\in \hat{E}(\calO_{K_{m-1}})\text{ for all }m\in S_{N,i'}^n \text{ and }\Tr_{K_n/K_N}x=0\right\}\\ =&\left\{x\in\hat{E}(\calO_{K_n}):P_{N,i}^n\circ\log_{\hat{E}}(x)=0\right\}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of the formal-group description
nodes.statement: By the comutative diagram above and Proposition~\ref{describingortho}, we have \[ \delta(x)\in H_{f,N,(i)}^1(K_n,T)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad i\circ\log_{\hat{E}}(x)\in \bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V)/\Fil^0\DD_{\cris}(V). \] Since $\log_{\hat{E}}$ is injective (by Assumption~\ref{assumptionptorsion}) and compatible with the trace maps, we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Chase the commutative diagram, using injectivity of $\log_{\hat{E}}$ and its trace compatibility.

nodes.name: $\Sel^{(i)}_N(E/L_n)$ and $\Sel^{(i)}_N(E/L_\infty)$
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a number field and $N$ is an integer such that $N\ge N(L_w,V)$ for all primes $w$of $L$ above $p$. For $i=1,2$, we define the Selmer groups \[ \Sel^{(i)}_N(E/L_n)=\ker\left(\Sel(E/L_n)\rTo \bigoplus_{w\mid p}\frac{H^1(L_{n,w},\Ep)}{\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{L_{n,w}})\otimes\Qp/\Zp }\right) \] for $n\ge N+1$. Moreover, we define \[ \Sel^{(i)}_N(E/L_\infty)=\varinjlim_{n\ge N+1}\Sel^{(i)}_N(E/L_n)=\ker\left(\Sel(E/L_\infty)\rTo \bigoplus_{\omega\mid p} \frac{H^1(L_{\infty,\omega},\Ep)}{\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{L_{\infty,\omega}})\otimes\Qp/\Zp} \right) \] where $\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{L_{\infty,\omega}})=\varinjlim \hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{L_{n,\omega\cap L_n}})$.
nodes.statement_short: Selmer groups defined by imposing the jumping conditions $\hat{E}_N^i$ at the primes above $p$.

nodes.name: Pontryagin dual of the finite-level jumping condition
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\Qp$ and $n\ge N(K,V)$. For $i=1,2$, the exact annihilator of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ under the Pontryagin duality \[ [\sim,\sim]: H^1(K_n,T)\times H^1(K_n,\Ep)\rTo\Qp\slash\Zp \] is isomorphic to $H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)\otimes\Qp/\Zp$ for $i=1,2$.
assumptions: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\Qp$ and $n\ge N(K,V)$.
conclusions: the exact annihilator of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ under the Pontryagin duality \[ [\sim,\sim]: H^1(K_n,T)\times H^1(K_n,\Ep)\rTo\Qp\slash\Zp \] is isomorphic to $H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)\otimes\Qp/\Zp$ for $i=1,2$.

nodes.name: Proof of the duality lemma
nodes.statement: This essentially follows from \cite[proofs of Lemma~8.17 and Proposition~8.18]{kobayashi03}. By definition, we have an exact sequence \[ 0\rTo H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)} \rTo H^1(K_n,T)\rTo\Hom\left(H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T),\Zp\right). \] On taking Pontryagin duals, we obtain a second exact sequence \[ H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)\otimes\Qp/\Zp\rTo H^1(K_n,\Ep)\rTo H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i),\vee}\rTo0. \] Therefore, it remains to show that the first map above is injective. But $[px,y]=p[x,y]$ for all $x,y\in H^1(K_n,T)$. This implies that if $x\in H^1(K_n,T)$ such that $px\in H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$, then $x\in H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Dualize the defining exact sequence and check injectivity of the first map from $p$-linearity of the pairing.

nodes.name: Pontryagin dual in terms of $\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{K_n})$
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\Qp$ and $n\ge N(K,V)$. For $i=1,2$, the exact annihilator of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ under the Pontryagin duality is isomorphic to $\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{K_{n}})\otimes\Qp/\Zp$ for $i=1,2$.
assumptions: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\Qp$ and $n\ge N(K,V)$.
conclusions: the exact annihilator of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ under the Pontryagin duality is isomorphic to $\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{K_{n}})\otimes\Qp/\Zp$ for $i=1,2$.

nodes.name: Proof of the formal-group duality
nodes.statement: This follows immediately from Corollary~\ref{rewrite} and Lemma~\ref{duals}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the formal-group description with the duality lemma.

nodes.name: The two definitions of signed Selmer groups coincide
nodes.statement: The two definitions of signed Selmer groups coincide, namely, \[ \Sel^{(i)}_N(E/L_\infty)=\Sel^i(E/L_\infty) \] for $i=1,2$.
assumptions: Throughout this section, we continue to assume that Assumption~\ref{assumptionptorsion} holds at all the primes of $L$ above $p$.
conclusions: The two definitions of signed Selmer groups coincide, namely, \[ \Sel^{(i)}_N(E/L_\infty)=\Sel^i(E/L_\infty) \] for $i=1,2$.

nodes.name: Proof that the two definitions agree
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that for any finite extensions $K$ of $\Qp$, we have \[ \varinjlim_n\frac{H^1(K_{n},\Ep)}{H^1_{f,i}(K_{n},\Ep)}\cong\varinjlim_{n\ge N+1}\frac{H^1(K_{n},\Ep)}{\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{K_{n}})\otimes\Qp/\Zp} \] where $N\ge N(K,V)$. On taking Pontryagin duals, this is equivalent to showing \[ \varprojlim H^1(K_n,T)^{i}\cong\varprojlim H^1_N(K_n,T)^{(i)} \] by Corollary~\ref{orthdual}. Therefore, we are done by Corollary~\ref{sameinv}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a local statement, dualize with the orthogonality corollary, and apply the inverse-limit description.

nodes.name: $\Sel^i(E/L_\infty)$ over a $p$-adic Lie extension and $X_i(E\slash L_\infty)$
nodes.statement: For $i=1,2$, we define $\Sel^i(E/L_\infty):=\varinjlim_m\Sel^i(E/L^{(m)}_\infty)$ for $=1,2$ and write \[ X_i(E\slash L_\infty)=\Hom_{\mathrm{cts}}\left(\Sel^i(E\slash L_\infty),\QQ_p\slash\ZZ_p\right). \]

nodes.name: The category $\mathfrak{M}_H(G)$
nodes.statement: Denote by $\mathfrak{M}_H(G)$ the category of finitely generated $\Lambda(G)$-modules $M$ for which $M\slash M(p)$ is finitely generated over $\Lambda(H)$. Here $M(p)$ denotes the $p$-torsion part of $M$.

nodes.name: Supersingular $\mathfrak{M}_H(G)$-conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\QQ$ with good supersingular reduction at $p$ and $a_p=0$. Let $L_\infty$ be a $p$-adic Lie extension of $\QQ$ containing $\QQ(\mu_{p^\infty})$. Define the Galois groups $G=\Gal(L_\infty\slash\QQ)$ and $H=\Gal(L_\infty\slash \QQ(\mu_p))$. Then $X_i(E\slash L_\infty)\in\mathfrak{M}_H(G)$ for $i=1,2$.
nodes.statement_short: The duals of the signed Selmer groups over a $p$-adic Lie extension should lie in $\mathfrak{M}_H(G)$.
assumptions: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\QQ$ with good supersingular reduction at $p$ and $a_p=0$.
Let $L_\infty$ be a $p$-adic Lie extension of $\QQ$ containing $\QQ(\mu_{p^\infty})$.
Define the Galois groups $G=\Gal(L_\infty\slash\QQ)$ and $H=\Gal(L_\infty\slash \QQ(\mu_p))$.

nodes.name: Control conjecture for the signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\QQ$ with good supersingular reduction at $p$ and $a_p=0$. Let $L_\infty$ be a $p$-adic Lie extension of $\QQ$ containing $\QQ(\mu_{p^\infty})$, and let $H=\Gal(L_\infty\slash \QQ(\mu_{p^\infty}))$. Assume also that $E(L_{v,\infty})$ has no $p$-torsion for any prime $v$ of $L$ above $p$. Then for $i=1,2$, the kernel and cokernel of the restriction map \[ \Sel^i(E\slash \QQ_\infty)\rTo \Sel^i(E\slash L_\infty)^H \] are cofinitely generated $\ZZ_p$-modules.
nodes.statement_short: Restriction from $\QQ_\infty$ to $L_\infty$ should have cofinitely generated kernel and cokernel.
assumptions: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\QQ$ with good supersingular reduction at $p$ and $a_p=0$.
Let $L_\infty$ be a $p$-adic Lie extension of $\QQ$ containing $\QQ(\mu_{p^\infty})$, and let $H=\Gal(L_\infty\slash \QQ(\mu_{p^\infty}))$.
Assume also that $E(L_{v,\infty})$ has no $p$-torsion for any prime $v$ of $L$ above $p$.
conclusions: Then for $i=1,2$, the kernel and cokernel of the restriction map \[ \Sel^i(E\slash \QQ_\infty)\rTo \Sel^i(E\slash L_\infty)^H \] are cofinitely generated $\ZZ_p$-modules.

nodes.name: Poitou-Tate exact sequences for the signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement: By \cite[\S A.3]{perrinriou95}, there are two exact sequences \begin{align} &0\rightarrow\Sel^i(E/\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo H^1(G_S(\QQ(\mu_{p^n})),\Ep)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f}J_v^i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo H^1_i(\QQ,T)^\vee\rTo\cdots\\ &0\rightarrow H^1_i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}),T)\rTo^{f_n}H^1(G_S(\QQ(\mu_{p^n})),\Ep)\rTo^{g_n}\bigoplus_{v\in S_f}I_v^i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo\cdots \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Two Poitou-Tate sequences relating $\Sel^i$, global cohomology and the local quotients $J_v^i$, $I_v^i$.

nodes.name: Surjectivity onto the finite local terms
nodes.statement: The natural map \[ H^1\big(G_S(\QQ_\infty),\Ep\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f} J_v^i(\QQ_\infty) \] is surjective.
assumptions: To simplify the notation, let $\QQ_\infty=\QQ(\mu_{p^\infty})$.
Write $S_f$ for the set of finite places of $S$ and let $I_v^i$ be as defined in Section~\ref{supersingular}.
conclusions: The natural map \[ H^1\big(G_S(\QQ_\infty),\Ep\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f} J_v^i(\QQ_\infty) \] is surjective.

nodes.name: Proof of the surjectivity lemma
nodes.statement: On taking inverse limit, we have \[ \varprojlim_n\Big( \bigoplus_{v\in S_f}I_v^i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))\Big) = \frac{H^1_{\Iw}(\Qp,T)}{H^1_{\Iw}(\Qp,T)^i} \] and $\displaystyle\varprojlim_n g_n$ is injective by \cite[Theorem~7.3]{kobayashi03}. Therefore, on taking inverse limit in \eqref{secondpt}, we have \[\varprojlim_n H^1_i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}),T)=0,\] which implies that $\displaystyle\varinjlim_n H^1_i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}),T)^\vee=0$. Therefore, on taking direct limit in \eqref{firstpt}, we have an exact sequence \[ 0\rTo\Sel^i(E/\QQ_\infty)\rTo H^1\big(G_S(\QQ_\infty),\Ep\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f} J_v^i(\QQ_\infty)\rTo 0 \] and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Take inverse limits in the second Poitou-Tate sequence to kill $H^1_i$, then take direct limits in the first.

nodes.name: Surjectivity onto all local terms
nodes.statement: The natural map \[ H^1\big(G_S(\QQ_\infty),\Ep\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S} J_v^i(\QQ_\infty) \] is surjective.
assumptions: To simplify the notation, let $\QQ_\infty=\QQ(\mu_{p^\infty})$.
This follows as $J_v^i(\QQ_\infty)=0$ for $p\neq2$ if $v$ is an infinite prime.

nodes.name: Proof of the corollary on surjectivity
nodes.statement: This follows as $J_v^i(\QQ_\infty)=0$ for $p\neq2$ if $v$ is an infinite prime.
nodes.statement_short: The infinite place contributes nothing since $p\neq2$.

nodes.name: Snake-lemma sequence for the fundamental diagram
nodes.statement: Applying the snake lemma gives a long exact sequence \[ 0 \rTo \ker(\alpha) \rTo \ker(\beta) \rTo \ker(\gamma) \rTo \coker(\alpha)\rTo \coker(\beta).\]
nodes.statement_short: The kernels and cokernels of $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ in the fundamental diagram fit into a six-term exact sequence.

nodes.name: Cofinite generation of $H^1(\mathcal{H},\hat{E}^i_N(\calO_{K_\infty}))$
nodes.statement: The cohomological group $H^1\left(\mathcal{H},\hat{E}^i_N(\calO_{K_\infty})\right)$ is a cofinitely generated $\Zp$-module.
assumptions: Let $K$ be the completion of $L$ at such a prime, and write $\mathcal{H}$ for the Galois group $\Gal(K_\infty\slash \QQ_{p,\infty})$.
conclusions: The cohomological group $H^1\left(\mathcal{H},\hat{E}^i_N(\calO_{K_\infty})\right)$ is a cofinitely generated $\Zp$-module.

nodes.name: Rescale $\bar{n}_2$ and record the new matrix
nodes.statement: If we let $\bar{n}_1'=\bar{n}_1$ and $\bar{n}_2'=v\bar{n}_2$ where $v\in(\BB_{\Qp}^+)^\times$, then $\bar{n}_1',\bar{n}_2'$ is also a basis of $\NN(V(-1))$. The matrix of $\vp$ with respect to this basis is of the form \[ P'=\begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \star \\ 0 & v^{-1}\vp(v)uq \end{pmatrix}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Replace $\bar{n}_2$ by $v\bar{n}_2$ for a unit $v$ and compute the resulting matrix $P'$ of $\vp$.

nodes.name: Convergence of the correcting product
nodes.statement: Note that $\alpha u\equiv1\mod\pi$ implies that $\vp^n(\alpha u)\rightarrow 1$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the product $\prod_{n\ge0}\vp^n(\alpha u)$ converges to an element $u'\in(\BB_{\Qp}^+)^\times$.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\prod_{n\ge0}\vp^n(\alpha u)$ converges to a unit $u'$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Choice of $v=u'$
nodes.statement: Since $u'\vp(u')^{-1}=\alpha u$, we deduce that $P'$ is of the required form if we take $v=u'$.
nodes.statement_short: Take $v=u'$ to put $P'$ in the required form.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Compute $\Col_2$
nodes.statement: By \eqref{colemanmaps}, we have $\Col_2(x)=\alpha x_2-\vp(x_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Read $\Col_2(x)=\alpha x_2-\vp(x_2)$ off the defining identity.

nodes.name: Shape of $M$
nodes.statement: Moreover, $M$ is lower triangular with $\alpha\frac{t}{\pi q}$ and $\alpha^{-1}$ on the diagonal.
nodes.statement_short: Note that $M$ is lower triangular with invertible diagonal entries.

nodes.name: Equality of the two kernels
nodes.statement: Therefore, $\ker(\underline{\Col}_2)=\ker(\Col_2)$ and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude $\ker(\underline{\Col}_2)=\ker(\Col_2)$.

nodes.name: Case $x\in\Brig$
nodes.statement:
If $x\in \Brig$, then we can substitute $\pi=e^t-1$ to write $x$ of the form $\sum_{n\geq 0}c_nt^n$ with $c_n\in\QQ_p$. Since $\vp(t)=pt$, it is clear from this description that for any $a
eq 1$ and $x
e0$, we have $\vp(x)
eq ax$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $x$ in powers of $t$ and use $\vp(t)=pt$ to rule out $\vp(x)=ax$.

nodes.name: Case of a finite overconvergence level
nodes.statement: Let $x\in\BB^\dagger_{\rig,\Qp}-\Brig$. Assume that there exists $n\ge 0$ be such that $x\in \BB^{\dagger,n}_{\rig,\QQ_p}$ and $x\not\in \BB^{\dagger,n-1}_{\rig,\QQ_p}$. Then $\vp(x)\in \BB^{\dagger,n+1}_{\rig,\QQ_p}-\BB^{\dagger,n}_{\rig,\QQ_p}$, so $\vp(x)\neq a x$.
nodes.statement_short: If $x$ has exact level $n$ then $\vp(x)$ has level $n+1$, so they cannot be proportional.

nodes.name: Case of all levels but not in $\Brig$
nodes.statement:
If $x\in\BB^{\dagger,n}_{ig,\QQ_p}$ for all $n\ge0$ and $x
ot\in\Brig$, then $\vp^{-1}(x)$ converges in $\BB^+_{\mathrm{dR}}$, so if we write $x=f(\pi)$, then $f(T)$ does not have a pole at $\varepsilon^{(1)}-1$. But $f(T)$ has a pole at $T=0$ as $x
ot\in\Brig$, so $f ig( (T+1)^p-1 ig)$ has poles at the $\{(\varepsilon^{(1)})^i-1:0\leq i<p\}$. Hence $\vp(x)
eq ax$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare poles of $f(T)$ and $f((T+1)^p-1)$ at $p$-power roots of unity.

nodes.name: Galois descent from $K$ to $\QQ_p$
nodes.statement: Assume now that $x\in \BB^\dagger_{\rig,K}$ satisfies $\vp(x)=ax$, and that $x\not\in \BB^{\dagger}_{\rig,\QQ_p}$. On replacing $K$ by its Galois closure, if necessary, we may assume that $K\slash\QQ_p$, and hence $K_{\infty}\slash\QQ_{p,\infty}$, are Galois. Let $H=\Gal(K_{\infty}\slash \QQ_{p,\infty})$. Since $\vp$ is $H$-equivariant, $\sigma(x)$ also satisfies~\eqref{nosolution} for all $\sigma\in H$. More generally, if $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_i\in H$, then $y=\sigma_1(x_2)\dots\sigma_i(x_2)$ satisfies $a^iy=\vp(y)$. The coefficients of the polynomial \[ f(Y)=\prod_{\sigma\in H} (Y-\sigma(x))\] are elements in $\BB^{\dagger}_{\rig,\QQ_p}$ which satisfy an equation of the form~\eqref{nosolution}, so they must all be zero by the above argument. But the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\BB^\dagger_{\rig,\QQ_p}$ divides $f(Y)$, which gives a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Form $\prod_{\sigma\in H}(Y-\sigma(x))$, force its coefficients to vanish, and contradict minimality of the minimal polynomial.

nodes.name: Rational identification of $H^1_{\Iw}(L_\nu,\hat{T})$
nodes.statement_short: Use $V^{H_{L_\nu}}=0$ plus Perrin-Riou and Bloch-Kato to identify $H^1_{\Iw}(L_\nu,\hat{T})\otimes\Qp$ with $\varprojlim H^1_f\otimes\Qp$.

nodes.name: Remove the rationalisation
nodes.statement_short: Torsion-freeness of the relevant quotients upgrades the rational identity to an integral one.

nodes.name: Dualize to compare the local terms
nodes.statement: On taking Pontryagin duals, we have $J_\nu^2(L_\infty)=J_\nu(L_\infty)$, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Dualizing gives $J_\nu^2(L_\infty)=J_\nu(L_\infty)$, hence the two Selmer groups agree.

nodes.name: Laurent-series case
nodes.statement: Firstly, we assume that $x\in\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]$. We write $\sigma$ for the Frobenious in $\Gal(K'/\Qp)$. Let \[ F(X)=\sum_{m\ge -r}b_mX^m\in\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![X]\!][X^{-1}] \] such that $F(\pi_K)=x$. For $i=1,\ldots,[K':\Qp]$, write \[ F_i(X)=\sum_{m\ge -r}\sigma^i(b_m)X^m.\] Then $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)=F_i(\pi_{n})$, where $i+n\equiv0\mod[K':\Qp]$ and $\pi_n=\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(\pi_K)$. Therefore, there exists an $i$ such that $F_i$ has infinitely many zeros. But $F_i\in X^{-r}\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![X]\!]$, so $F_i=0$ by the Weierstrass preparation theorem. This implies that $b_m=0$ for all $m$, so $x=0$.
nodes.statement_short: For $x$ a Laurent series, Weierstrass preparation forces the twisted series $F_i$ to vanish identically.

nodes.name: Pass to the $p$-adic completion
nodes.statement: To conclude, note that if $n\ge N$, $\{x\in\AA^{\dagger,N}_K:\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)=0\}$ is a closed set of $\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ under the $p$-adic topology and $\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ is the $p$-adic completion of $\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]\cap\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ by Lemma~\ref{completion}.
nodes.statement_short: The vanishing locus is closed, so the result extends to all of $\AA^{\dagger,N}_K$ by Lemma completion.

nodes.name: Choose $n$ and expand $x$
nodes.statement: We let $n$ be an integer such that $[K_n:K_{n-1}]=p$ and $n\ge a(K)+1$ where $a(K)$ is the integer as in \cite[Proposition~III.2.1]{cherbonniercolmez99}. Write \[ x=\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}[\varepsilon]^i\vp(x_i) \] where $x_i\in\BB_{K}^{\dagger,n-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take $n$ large and write $x=\sum_i[\varepsilon]^i\vp(x_i)$.

nodes.name: Compute the trace term by term
nodes.statement: Then, \[ \theta\circ\vp^{-n+1}(x_i)\in K_{n-1} \] for all $i$. Therefore, \begin{eqnarray*} \Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ \theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x)&=&\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}\zeta_{p^n}^i\theta\circ\vp^{1-n}(x_i)\right)\\ &=&p\theta\circ\vp^{1-n}(x_0). \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Only the $i=0$ term survives the trace, giving $p\theta\circ\vp^{1-n}(x_0)$.

nodes.name: Match with $\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}$
nodes.statement: But we have $\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}(x)=p\vp(x_0)$, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Match with $\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}(x)=p\vp(x_0)$.

nodes.name: Derive the $\log^\pm$ identities
nodes.statement: By definitions, we have $\vp(\log^+(1+\pi))=\frac{p}{q}\log^-(1+\pi)$ and $\vp(\log^-(1+\pi))=\log^+(1+\pi)$, and that similar relations hold when replacing $\vp$ by $\psi$. The relations \eqref{basechange} therefore imply that \begin{eqnarray} \vp(x_1)+p\psi(x_1)&=&\left(\vp(x_1')+\psi(qx_1')\right)\log^+(1+\pi);\\ \vp(x_2)+p\psi(x_2)&=&\left(\vp(x_2')+q\psi(x_2')\right)p/q\log^-(1+\pi). \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Translate \eqref{basechange} into formulas for $\vp(x_i)+p\psi(x_i)$ in terms of $\log^\pm(1+\pi)$.

nodes.name: Even $n$ gives the $x_1$ relation
nodes.statement: If $n\ge 2$ is an even integer, then $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}\left(\log^+(1+\pi)\right)=0$. Therefore, \eqref{log1} implies that \[ \theta\circ\vp^{-n+1}(x_1)+\theta\circ\vp^{-n-1}\left(p\vp\circ\psi(x_1)\right)=0. \] Recall that $p\vp\circ\psi=\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}$, so Lemma~\ref{comptrace} implies the first part of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(\log^+(1+\pi))=0$ and the trace-compatibility lemma.

nodes.name: Odd $n$ gives the $x_2$ relation
nodes.statement: Similarly, the second half the lemma follows from \eqref{log2} and the fact that \[\theta\circ\vp^{-n}\left(p/q\log^-(1+\pi)\right)=0\] for all odd integers $n\ge 3$.
nodes.statement_short: The symmetric argument with $p/q\log^-(1+\pi)$ gives the second relation.

nodes.name: Forward implication
nodes.statement: If $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$, then \[ \vp^2(x_i)=-p\vp\circ\psi(x_i)=-\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}(x_i). \] On applying $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}$ to both sides, we have by Lemma~\ref{comptrace} that \[ \theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_i)=-\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_i) \] as required.
nodes.statement_short: Apply $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}$ to $\vp^2(x_i)=-\Tr_{\BB/\vp(\BB)}(x_i)$ and use the trace lemma.

nodes.name: Converse implication
nodes.statement: Conversely, we assume that \[ \Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_i)=-\theta\circ\vp^{2-n}(x_i) \] for all $n\ge N+2$. Then $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}\left(\vp(x_i)+p\psi(x_i)\right)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{comptrace}. Our assumption implies that $\vp(x_1')+\psi(qx_1')=0$ for $i=1$ and $\vp(x_2')+q\psi(x_2')=0$ for $i=2$ by Lemma~\ref{vanish} and the equations \eqref{log1} and \eqref{log2}. Therefore, we have $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^i$ as required.
nodes.statement_short: The trace relations force $\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(\vp(x_i)+p\psi(x_i))=0$, and the vanishing lemma recovers the defining condition.

nodes.name: Invoke the Cherbonnier-Colmez formula
nodes.statement: By \cite[Th\'eor\`eme IV.2.1]{cherbonniercolmez99}, \[ \exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)= \partial_V\circ \vp^{-n}(x)\] for all $n\geq N$.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}$ by $\partial_V\circ\vp^{-n}$.

nodes.name: Split by the parity of $n$
nodes.statement: Since \[ \partial_V\circ \vp^{-n}(x)=\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_1)\vp^{-n}(v_1)+\theta\circ\vp^{-n}(x_2)\vp^{-n}(v_2)\] and the image of $\exp^*_{K_n}$ lies in $K_n\otimes{\Fil}^0\DD_{\cris}(V)$, it follows that \[ \exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)= \begin{cases} (-1)^mp^{-m}\theta\circ\vp^{-2m}(x_1)v_1 & \text{ if $n=2m\ge N$}, \\ (-1)^mp^{-m}\theta\circ\vp^{-(2m+1)}(x_2)v_1 & \text{ if $n=2m+1\ge N$}. \end{cases} \]
nodes.statement_short: Because the image lies in $\Fil^0\DD_{\cris}(V)$, only $x_1$ (even $n$) or $x_2$ (odd $n$) contributes.

nodes.name: Restate the signed condition as a trace relation
nodes.statement: Extend the trace map $\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}$ to the map $\Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\mathrm{id}$ on $K_n\otimes_{\Qp}\DD_{\cris}(V)$. Then, $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^1$ if and only if \[ \Tr_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}(x)=p^{-1}\exp^*_{K_{n-2}}\circ h^1_{\Iw,{n-2}}(x) \] for all even $n\ge N+2$.
nodes.statement_short: Membership in $H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^1$ becomes a relation between consecutive levels of $\exp^*\circ h^1_{\Iw,n}$.

nodes.name: Shift indices via corestriction compatibility
nodes.statement: But \[ \Tr_{K_m\slash K_{m-1}}\circ \exp^*_{K_{m}} =\exp^*_{K_{m-1}}\circ {\cor}_{K_m\slash K_{m-1}} \] for all $m\ge0$, so we deduce that $x\in H^1_{\Iw}(K,T)^1$ if and only if \[ \exp^*_{K_{n-1}}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n-1}(x)=p^{-1}\Tr_{K_{n-1}/K_{n-2}}\circ\exp^*_{K_{n-1}}\circ h^1_{\Iw,n-1}(x) \] for all even $n\ge N-2$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\Tr\circ\exp^*=\exp^*\circ\cor$ to rewrite the criterion at level $n-1$.

nodes.name: Rewrite as an annihilator
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{3des}, we have \begin{equation} H^1_{f,N,(1)}(K_n,T)=\left(\left(\exp^*_{K_n}\right)^{-1}\left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\cdot v_1\right)\right)^{\bot_{[,]}} \end{equation} where $(\star)^{\bot_{[,]}}$ denotes the exact annihilator of $\star$ under the pairing $[\sim,\sim]$.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the preimage description of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ into the annihilator.

nodes.name: Adjunction between $\exp$ and $\exp^*$
nodes.statement: But \[ [\exp_{K_n}(\sim),\sim]=\Tr_{K_n/\Qp}\langle\sim,\exp^*_{K_n}(\sim)\rangle. \] where $\langle\sim,\sim\rangle$ is the pairing \[ \langle\sim,\sim\rangle:\Big(K_n\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V)\Big)\times\Big(K_n\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V)\Big)\rightarrow K_n. \]
nodes.statement_short: Express the Tate pairing of $\exp_{K_n}(\cdot)$ through $\Tr_{K_n/\Qp}\langle\cdot,\exp^*_{K_n}(\cdot)\rangle$.

nodes.name: Translate to an orthogonal complement in $K_n$
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{equation} x\in\left(\left(\exp^*_{K_n}\right)^{-1}\left(\star\cdot v_1\right)\right)^{\bot_{[,]}}\quad\text{if and only if}\quad x\in\exp_{K_n}\left((\star)^\bot\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V)\right) \end{equation} where $(\star)^\bot$ denotes the orthogonal complement of $\star$ under the pairing \begin{align*} K_n\times K_n &\rightarrow \Qp\\ (x,y) &\mapsto \Tr_{K_n/\Qp}(xy). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Membership in the annihilator becomes membership in $\exp_{K_n}((\star)^\bot\otimes\DD_{\cris}(V))$.

nodes.name: Compute the complement
nodes.statement: By linear algebra, we have \[ \left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\right)^\bot=\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}. \] Hence the result on combining \eqref{E} with \eqref{ortho}.
nodes.statement_short: Linear algebra identifies $(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{S_{N,i'}^n}K_m^{(0)})^\bot$ with $\bigoplus_{S_{N,i}^n}K_m^{(0)}$.

nodes.name: Set up the defining exact sequence
nodes.statement: This essentially follows from \cite[proofs of Lemma~8.17 and Proposition~8.18]{kobayashi03}. By definition, we have an exact sequence \[ 0\rTo H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)} \rTo H^1(K_n,T)\rTo\Hom\left(H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T),\Zp\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Write the exact sequence defining $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$, following Kobayashi.

nodes.name: Dualize and isolate the remaining point
nodes.statement: On taking Pontryagin duals, we obtain a second exact sequence \[ H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)\otimes\Qp/\Zp\rTo H^1(K_n,\Ep)\rTo H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i),\vee}\rTo0. \] Therefore, it remains to show that the first map above is injective.
nodes.statement_short: Pontryagin duality leaves only injectivity of the first map to check.

nodes.name: Injectivity from $p$-linearity
nodes.statement: But $[px,y]=p[x,y]$ for all $x,y\in H^1(K_n,T)$. This implies that if $x\in H^1(K_n,T)$ such that $px\in H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$, then $x\in H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Since $[px,y]=p[x,y]$, the subgroup $H^1_{f,N,(i)}$ is $p$-saturated, giving injectivity.

nodes.name: Reduce to a local comparison
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that for any finite extensions $K$ of $\Qp$, we have \[ \varinjlim_n\frac{H^1(K_{n},\Ep)}{H^1_{f,i}(K_{n},\Ep)}\cong\varinjlim_{n\ge N+1}\frac{H^1(K_{n},\Ep)}{\hat{E}_N^i(\calO_{K_{n}})\otimes\Qp/\Zp} \] where $N\ge N(K,V)$.
nodes.statement_short: It is enough to compare the two local quotients over each finite extension $K$ of $\Qp$.

nodes.name: Dualize using the orthogonality corollary
nodes.statement: On taking Pontryagin duals, this is equivalent to showing \[ \varprojlim H^1(K_n,T)^{i}\cong\varprojlim H^1_N(K_n,T)^{(i)} \] by Corollary~\ref{orthdual}.
nodes.statement_short: Dualizing turns the comparison into $\varprojlim H^1(K_n,T)^i\cong\varprojlim H^1_N(K_n,T)^{(i)}$.

nodes.name: Apply the inverse-limit description
nodes.statement: Therefore, we are done by Corollary~\ref{sameinv}.
nodes.statement_short: Cite Corollary sameinv.

nodes.name: Identify the inverse limit of the local terms
nodes.statement: On taking inverse limit, we have \[ \varprojlim_n\Big( \bigoplus_{v\in S_f}I_v^i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}))\Big) = \frac{H^1_{\Iw}(\Qp,T)}{H^1_{\Iw}(\Qp,T)^i} \] and $\displaystyle\varprojlim_n g_n$ is injective by \cite[Theorem~7.3]{kobayashi03}.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\varprojlim_n\bigoplus_v I_v^i$ and cite injectivity of $\varprojlim g_n$.

nodes.name: Vanishing of $\varprojlim H^1_i$
nodes.statement: Therefore, on taking inverse limit in \eqref{secondpt}, we have \[\varprojlim_n H^1_i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}),T)=0,\] which implies that $\displaystyle\varinjlim_n H^1_i(\QQ(\mu_{p^n}),T)^\vee=0$.
nodes.statement_short: The second Poitou-Tate sequence forces $\varprojlim_n H^1_i=0$, hence its dual limit vanishes.

nodes.name: Direct limit of the first sequence
nodes.statement: Therefore, on taking direct limit in \eqref{firstpt}, we have an exact sequence \[ 0\rTo\Sel^i(E/\QQ_\infty)\rTo H^1\big(G_S(\QQ_\infty),\Ep\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f} J_v^i(\QQ_\infty)\rTo 0 \] and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: The first Poitou-Tate sequence then ends in $0$, which is the asserted surjectivity.
